feed.title: TJX CEO: Distribution model will help weather El Niño
feed.summary: TJX Companies CEO Ernie Herrman stated that the off-price retailer's warehouse distribution model, also known as the "hold and flow" model, provides flexibility to manage inventory in response to unpredictable events like El Niño. This strategy allows TJX to store goods in warehouses and dispatch them to stores based on real-time data, weather patterns, and demand, giving them better control than traditional retailers who often send inventory directly to stores. This approach contrasts with the "flow-through" model where inventory quickly moves through distribution centers, and some retailers use a hybrid approach depending on product variability.

feed.title: T-Mobile’s $85 Billion Debt Load Won’t Feel the Fed’s Rate Hike the Way Wall Street Thinks
feed.summary: T-Mobile's substantial debt load is largely insulated from recent Federal Reserve rate hikes because most of its $86.9 billion debt consists of fixed-rate notes, not floating-rate debt. The company's strong free cash flow, projected at $18.4 to $18.8 billion for 2026, further mitigates the impact of any incremental interest costs, positioning T-Mobile more favorably than some analysts suggest.

feed.title: Merck Launches Your Hive of Whole Health to Support Whole Person Care for People Living With HIV
feed.summary: Merck has launched "Your Hive of Whole Health," a multi-year educational program designed to help people living with HIV build support networks for their physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being. Unveiled at the 2026 U.S. Conference on HIV/AIDS (USCHA), the initiative emphasizes whole-person care beyond viral suppression, with actress and advocate Debbie Allen joining the launch. The program provides tools and resources for individuals to create personalized "Hives" of care, involving healthcare providers, community advocates, family, and peers.
